patterns: Personifying the brain as a relational character (e.g., cute, stressed, or tricked) rather than just an anatomical organ
Visually proving an immediate optical or cognitive illusion that the viewer tests on themselves in real time
Action-oriented 'mind reading' and practical handwriting/body language profiling tips
Direct second-person addressing ('Your Brain', 'You') framed around everyday sensory experiences like coffee, sleeping, or seeing
Explaining bizarre brain mechanics using relatable analogies, like car parts or daily electronics
title_formulas: How Your Brain Secrets [Specific Sensory Trick or Habit] [Emoji]
This Classic Psychology Trick Shows How Your [Mind/Brain] Works [Emoji]
What [Everyday Substance or Habit] Really Does To Your Mind [Emoji]
opening_3s: Ask the viewer to stare at a static classic illusion while promising their perception will warp in 5 seconds
Show a historical 19th-century diagram of a brain performing an everyday modern chore
State a surprising historical psychological premise about how we process hand gestures while demonstrating it visually
comment_themes: Deep affection for animated or personified visual depictions of cognitive processes
A desire to test psychological concepts immediately on friends, family, or themselves
Debating the accuracy of everyday analogies used to explain complex mental phenomena
Humorous reactions to realization of their own subconscious habits and mood shifts
avoid: Direct medical advice, clinical diagnoses, or promising cures for neurological conditions
Gory or graphic visual depictions of biological trauma and brain injuries
Sensationalized claims about unlocking 100% brain power or instant mind control
